translation_notes: The stratum's read: `not any(graph.subjects(None, s))` -> `not m{ ?x ?p {s} }` ("is s the object of any triple"). The predicate wildcard cannot be `[]` in predicate position, so two throwaway variables ?x ?p are named, which the original did not need; `@graph graph` at the top of the function.

`set(graph.subjects())` stays: a full scan with no selection, for which the language reference says to keep the rdflib call (m{ ?s ?p ?o } yields triples, not subjects, and would need a comprehension).

`self` is the JSON-LD Converter, whose process_subject is out of the region: the driver passes a Recorder stub (in driver.py, same on both sides) that logs the subject and puts a node in nodemap, so both the returned list and the dispatched subjects are compared. Fixture: IRI subjects, an unreferenced bnode (processed), bnodes referenced by an IRI, by a bnode, through a cycle and in an rdf:type object position (skipped); plus an empty graph. Mutants killed: `not` dropped, subject/object swapped, predicate fixed.
optimization_notes: Python: `not any(graph.subjects(None, s))` becomes `(None, None, s) not in graph` (Graph.__contains__ accepts None wildcards and stops at the first match, as any() did), which lets the condition fit on one line; the blank lines go. `isinstance(s, BNode)` stays: without it a Literal subject of a generalised graph would be dispatched. `set(graph.subjects())` is already the shortest form.

LD Python: the same lines, the containment test written `not m{ ?x ?p {s} }(graph)` with a call suffix instead of an `@graph graph` line; the two throwaway variables make it exactly as long as the Python containment test (notation ratio 1.0): the island is kept because it is not longer, and the measurement shows it gains nothing here. No exception to the symmetry rule.
header_optimization_notes: Python: Literal goes from the rdflib.term import.
LD Python: Literal goes from the rdflib.term import; no @prefix in the header.
